postgres_requirements.rationale: A real PostgreSQL probe is MANDATORY for this batch and both manifest paths are legitimately UNKNOWN because no implementing node exists yet — this manifest is a pre-implementation commitment, and naming a harness path that does not exist would be a fabricated fact. The authority's REAL_PG_CONTRACT section freezes six required probes: PG-1 (a RESTRICTIVE selected-org conjunct denies a non-selected organization's row to a subject who is a member of BOTH), PG-2 (current_setting('app.organization_id', true) resolves to the CALLER's value inside the SECURITY DEFINER can_write_evidence_object), PG-3 (an unset GUC yields zero rows and no writes), PG-4 (concurrent invitation acceptance and bootstrap are serialized WITHOUT user_single_active_membership), PG-5 (a dual-member subject scoped to organization A reads nothing from B), PG-6 (the founder-cardinality carrier refuses a second self-service founding while permitting historical NULL founded_by rows). Static reading of SQL text is NOT proof for any of the six: policy combination (PERMISSIVE OR versus RESTRICTIVE AND), definer GUC resolution, NULL-not-TRUE denial, concurrency serialization, and partial-index/NULL interaction are all runtime properties. HARNESS SHAPE, frozen here: a disposable cluster only, via pnpm db:audit:disposable — NEVER staging, NEVER production, NEVER the canonical local stack; a TWO-TENANT fixture carrying real rows in the non-selected organization, because a probe that returns zero rows merely for want of data proves nothing; and a TWO-PHASE construction, because the DUAL-MEMBER fixture required by PG-1 and PG-5 is impossible to build while user_single_active_membership exists and may only be constructed in a post-S7 phase inside the disposable cluster. Dropping the index early to make a fixture buildable is prohibited by DROP_LAST_RULE.prohibited_shortcuts.

sentinels.purpose: A uniquely-valued row planted in the NON-SELECTED organization B. It must never appear in any result set, log line, error payload, PDF or report produced by a request scoped to organization A. Its purpose is to make cross-tenant leakage assertable by identity rather than by row count — a count-based assertion cannot distinguish 'denied' from 'no such row'.

A historical organization fixture whose ONLY founder signal is invited_by IS NULL. Its purpose is to prove the MO-11 hard prohibition: after backfill its founded_by must still be NULL. If any backfill implementation ever attributes a founder to this fixture, M-5 fails.

An organization set to status='suspended' through the governed capability path. Its purpose is to prove SUSPENDED_ORG_BEHAVIOR D1/D3 — that it is absent from selection options and that a pre-existing carrier naming it is refused on the next request, rather than merely being cosmetically hidden in the UI.

A confirmed platform super_admin subject holding NO membership in the target organization. Its purpose is to prove the removal of the db/identity-context.ts:217 exemption (SC-3) and, in the same fixture, that the adjacent DB_IDENTITY_SUPER_ADMIN_CLAIM_REJECTED check survived that edit (M-7).

positive_controls.description: MANIFEST PRECONDITION, UNKNOWN BY CONSTRUCTION. The two known_conditions listed above are the only entries in docs/ops/ods/KNOWN_TEST_CONDITIONS_v1.0.0.json at AS_OF_HEAD, read directly from that file. Both are PRE_EXISTING_DEFERRED failures of tests/eval/stella-release/hosted-baseline-gate.test.ts caused by a rehearsal artefact recorded against an older baseline manifest; this batch adds units to db/hosted/baseline-manifest.ts and therefore changes the manifest digest they fingerprint. Their applicability to each implementing node is UNKNOWN and MUST be re-verified with pnpm ops:test-diff at that node's own base — it could NOT be run in the authoring worktree because node_modules is ABSENT. A node that observes a hosted-baseline-gate failure whose signature does NOT match these two fingerprints has found a NEW failure and must fail closed rather than classify it as known.

S1 / MO-10. organizations.founded_by exists as uuid NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT, and an organization founded through the CAP-05 bootstrap path after S1 carries founded_by set to the bootstrapping subject from the recorded founding act, not from inference.

S1 / MO-11. The backfill leaves founded_by NULL for every historical organization lacking deterministic founding provenance, and emits a reproducible count of rows-attributed and rows-left-NULL. A NULL outcome is recorded as an outcome, since MO-11's honesty requirement is only auditable if the non-attribution is itself recorded.
S2 / MO-04. Selecting an organization writes a session carrier with HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax and NO Max-Age and NO Expires, so the selection dies with the browser session.

S3 / MO-03 + MO-05. The request principal resolves the membership by the (user, SELECTED organization) pair rather than by pick-first over the user's active memberships, and re-derives that proof from live database state on EVERY request. This supersedes the .limit(1) at lib/auth/database-context.ts:219.
S3 / MO-06. The role used for every capability check is the role held in the SELECTED organization's membership, and a role held in another organization contributes nothing to it.
S3c / MO-12. A Stella interaction produced by a request scoped to organization A is attributed to A, and that attribution is rechecked at the database boundary rather than only in application code.

S4 / GUC_CONTRACT + RLS_TARGET. Tenant row authorization is the CONJUNCTION of membership-set inclusion (existing PERMISSIVE predicate, unchanged) and selected-organization equality (new conjunct, published AS RESTRICTIVE), and an ordinary in-scope read of the selected organization's own rows continues to succeed unchanged. Requires PG-1.

S4 / RLS_TARGET closed-world. The enumeration of welded tables is derived from live pg_policy catalog state under the disposable harness, and every table carrying organization_id is either welded or explicitly classified out of scope with a recorded reason. The number 45 measured at AS_OF_HEAD is a TEXT OCCURRENCE COUNT in db/baseline/stella_g2_schema.sql and must not be used as a policy count.

S4 / STORAGE_V1_BOUNDARY. An evidence-object write permitted for the selected organization still succeeds after can_write_evidence_object is welded to the selected-org conjunct, and stella_0019's own verification assertions (that it recreates no policy on storage.objects, and that insert_evidence and delete_evidence still call the helper) are preserved rather than weakened. Requires PG-2.
S5 / MO-08. A platform super_admin retains full global reach over organizations through the /admin control plane WITHOUT constructing a tenant context, including over a suspended organization.

S6 / MO-02 + INVITATIONS. A subject holding an active membership in organization A accepts an invitation to organization B through the ordinary product invitation path and ends with TWO active memberships, without the acceptance changing the currently selected organization.

S6 / SS-01 ALLOWLIST_EXIT. A verified subject who appears on NO allowlist completes self-service organization founding successfully. Until this passes, ALLOWLIST_EXIT is not satisfied; a residual allowlist may exist only as an operator-controlled, DEFAULT-OFF control.

S6 / SS-02 + SI-7. Concurrent invitation acceptance and organization bootstrap remain serialized by an explicit DATABASE-level guarantee that does not depend on user_single_active_membership, and bootstrap remains deterministic and idempotent. Requires PG-4. An application-level read-then-write check does not satisfy this control.

S7 / MO-02. With user_single_active_membership dropped, a subject holds two active memberships and a request scoped to organization A functions normally in A. Requires PG-5. S7's diff contains exactly one index drop and nothing else.

S8 / GOLDEN_S8_CONTRACT. The existing commercial Golden E2E journey is RETAINED in full and EXTENDED: found A, accept an invitation to B, select A, complete a Golden step in A, switch to B, complete a step in B under B's role, with A's data absent throughout the B-scoped portion. The subject MUST hold DIFFERENT roles in A and B, since equal roles cannot detect cross-organization role-ceiling failures. No direct-SQL, test-only or seed shortcut may construct the second membership.

negative_controls.description: SC-1 / S3. A carrier naming an organization in which the subject holds no ACTIVE membership is REFUSED with failure code TENANCY_SELECTED_ORGANIZATION_NOT_A_MEMBER, and there is NO fallback to any other membership. The assertion is on the FAILURE CODE, not merely on the absence of the other organization's data — an assertion on absence alone cannot distinguish a refusal from a silent fallback that happened to return nothing.
SC-2 / S3. Membership revoked mid-session is refused on the NEXT request, with no grace window. A memoized or session-cached membership proof fails this control.

SC-3 / S5. A confirmed platform super_admin who is NOT an active member of the target organization is REFUSED on a tenant route, proving removal of the `&& !check.is_super_admin` exemption at db/identity-context.ts:217. Uses SENTINEL_SUPERADMIN_NON_MEMBER.

SC-4 and GUC_CONTRACT C5 / S4. THE PRIMARY NEGATIVE CONTROL OF THE BATCH. A subject who is an active member of BOTH organizations, scoped to A, cannot read or write SENTINEL_ORG_B_CANARY_ROW; and separately, a tenant-scoped query executed with app.organization_id UNSET returns zero rows and permits no writes. Requires PG-1 and PG-3. This control is what makes DROP_LAST safe: current_user_org_ids() (db/migrations/0031_rls_core.sql:25-37) returns EVERY active membership, so `= ANY(current_user_org_ids())` is a single-organization predicate only while the dropped index holds it to one element.

SC-4 / PROJECT_AUTHORIZATION / S4. Addressing a project id belonging to the NON-SELECTED organization is refused with TENANCY_CROSS_ORG_RESOURCE_REFUSED on the project-scoped routes, which at AS_OF_HEAD include the eight project and portfolio consumers of runWithOptionalOrganizationAccess measured in the companion authority's evidence anchor E15. Project ids are client-supplied, so this is reachable input, not a hypothetical.

SC-5 / S5. SENTINEL_SUSPENDED_ORG is absent from selection options, and a pre-existing carrier naming it is refused on the next request with TENANCY_ORGANIZATION_SUSPENDED — evaluated at revalidation time, not only at selection time.

SC-6 / S1. A second self-service founding attempt by the same subject is refused with TENANCY_FOUNDER_CARDINALITY_EXCEEDED and does NOT silently return the subject's existing organization; and the backfill leaves SENTINEL_FOUNDER_NULL_ORG's founded_by NULL. Requires PG-6.

SC-7 / S3c / MO-12. A Stella write asserting an organization other than the request's selected organization is refused AT THE DATABASE BOUNDARY. The refusal must hold with the membership ceiling absent, since MO-12 explicitly rejects a design in which the membership ceiling alone prevents ambiguous cross-scope attribution.

PI-3 / S1. A subject named in organizations.founded_by who holds NO active membership in that organization is refused tenant access. founded_by is traceability, never authorization; this control proves the two did not get wired together.

mutation_controls.description: Guarantee: the selected-org conjunct is RESTRICTIVE. Mutation: change it to PERMISSIVE. Must be caught by N-4 — a permissive policy combines with OR, so the non-selected organization's canary row becomes readable again. This is the exact regression shape already adjudicated as adversarial finding A2-F02 in docs/ops/capabilities/ADVERSARIAL_FINDINGS_ROUND2.md, which closed by converting nine capability policies to AS RESTRICTIVE.

Guarantee: the GUC is transaction-local. Mutation: change the third argument of set_config at db/identity-context.ts:180 from true to false. Must be caught by a control proving the selected scope does not survive into a subsequent transaction on a pooled connection.
Guarantee: per-request revalidation. Mutation: memoize the membership proof for the life of the session. Must be caught by N-2.

Guarantee: no fallback on refusal. Mutation: replace the TENANCY_SELECTED_ORGANIZATION_NOT_A_MEMBER throw with a fallback to the subject's first remaining membership. Must be caught by N-1, which is why N-1 asserts the failure code rather than data absence.

Guarantee: the MO-11 backfill prohibition. Mutation: add `invited_by IS NULL` as a backfill attribution predicate. Must be caught by N-7 via SENTINEL_FOUNDER_NULL_ORG, whose only founder signal is exactly that predicate.
Guarantee: founded_by grants nothing (PI-3). Mutation: add founded_by as a disjunct to any authorization predicate or RLS policy. Must be caught by N-9.

Guarantee: the DB_IDENTITY_SUPER_ADMIN_CLAIM_REJECTED check survives the S5 exemption removal (PI-10). Mutation: delete the branch at db/identity-context.ts:210-215 while editing the adjacent branch at :217. Must be caught by a control proving an unconfirmed super-admin claim is still rejected. This control exists because the likeliest S5 defect is removing too much from an adjacent line.

Guarantee: DROP_LAST ordering. Mutation: drop user_single_active_membership in any node earlier than S7, or as an incidental part of a larger diff. Must be caught by a control asserting the index is PRESENT at the end of every node S1 through S6, and that S7's diff contains exactly one index drop and no other change.
